Simulate a tiered twenty-player tennis league

Source: R/tennis_tiered_toy.R
tennis_tiered_toy.Rd

Simulate a complete league with user-specified block strengths and sizes. A common random permutation shuffles both axes.

Usage

tennis_tiered_toy(
  matches_per_pair = 20L,
  seed = 101L,
  n_blocks = length(latent_strength),
  latent_strength = c(12, 6, 2, 1),
  players_per_block = 5L,
  item_labels = NULL,
  format = c("data", "edgelist")
)

Arguments

matches_per_pair

Positive integer number of matches for each pair.

seed

Integer random seed, or NULL to use the current random state.

n_blocks

Positive integer number of generating blocks.

latent_strength

Positive vector with one strength per generating block. The default c(12, 6, 2, 1) is on the same scale as the default Gamma prior and gives tiers that are separable but not perfectly so.

players_per_block

Positive integer block sizes, either one common size or a vector of length n_blocks.

item_labels

Optional unique names for all players.

format

Return validated data (default) or a winner/loser/count edge list.

Value

A btsbm_pairwise_data object, or an edge-list data frame, with generating groups and strengths stored in its truth attribute. All observations are synthetic.
